newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thai intervention may drive buyers to others-trade.
newsitem.headline: Thai intervention may drive buyers to others-trade.

text.p: The steep price set by the Thai government as it intervenes in the regional rubber market may prompt some buyers to switch to Indonesian or Malaysian-origins, Singapore rubber dealers said on Tuesday.
Thailand raised its intervention price recently to 29 baht a kg from 27.50 baht previously as it sought to molify Thai rubber farmers angry over the current low price of rubber.

"If they maintain this high price, there's every reason for buyers to switch to either SIR or SMR rubber. This is one consequence of the decision by Thailand to intervene in the market," a trader said.

SIR rubber is produced by Indonesia while SMR comes from Malaysia. Dealers in Singapore said they have not seen large amounts of switching, but said it is only a matter of time before buyers decide prices of the RSS3 grade rubber produced by Thailand is too high.
Trading in the Singapore rubber market was very thin.
"We issued our prices, but nobody is hitting us. It's very quiet," one dealer said.
At 0945 GMT, July RSS3 was indicated at 115.00 U.S. cents a kg from 114.50 cents. All contracts of the TSR20 were untraded. -- Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
